name: What a vaccine actually does to the immune system
scope: The MECHANISM honored, built out of named discoveries rather than a textbook definition. T1: Christmas night 1891 in Berlin, Emil von Behring injected a dying diphtheria child with blood SERUM taken from an immunized animal, and the child lived -- the protection was in the clear liquid of another creature's blood, something that animal's body had manufactured (first Nobel in Medicine, 1901). T2: Behring's partner Kitasato Shibasaburo co-authored the 1890 antitoxin paper and was left off the Nobel -- an honest credit rung. T2: the ANTIGEN PREVIEW -- a vaccine shows the body a killed copy or a harmless fragment, and the body does not build a new weapon; it already carries a lymphocyte for almost any shape and the preview simply lets the matching ones multiply (Burnet and Talmage's clonal-selection idea, 1957). T3: Paul Ehrlich's 1897 'side-chain' drawings -- he sketched receptors on cells that lock onto a toxin and are then shed into the blood as free antibodies; wrong in detail, right in the essential picture, Nobel 1908. T3: MEMORY -- why a second meeting is faster and larger: memory B and T cells persist for decades, which is why chickenpox at six still protects at sixty. T4: Susumu Tonegawa's puzzle -- a few hundred genes cannot spell billions of antibodies; in 1976-78 he showed that the antibody genes are physically CUT AND RESHUFFLED inside each developing B cell (Nobel 1987). T4: ADJUVANTS -- Alexander Glenny found in 1926 that aluminium salts made a purified antigen provoke a far bigger response; the mechanism of why aluminium works was argued over into the 2000s (an honest open corner). T5: why a measles shot lasts and a flu shot expires -- Maurice Hilleman's antigenic DRIFT and SHIFT: influenza rewrites its surface coat continuously, measles barely changes, so memory keeps matching one and loses the other. T5: the honest limit built into the mechanism -- the injected killed polio vaccine raises serum IgG that stops the virus reaching nerves, but raises little gut IgA, so a fully protected child can still carry and pass the virus on; protection-from-disease and blocking-transmission are two different things.
source: grokipedia.com/page/Adaptive_immune_system (specificity, diversity, memory, somatic recombination, clonal expansion, 'foundation of vaccination'); grokipedia.com/page/Maurice_Hilleman (antigenic drift vs shift, >40 vaccines, National Medal of Science 1988); grokipedia.com/page/Polio_vaccine (IPV serum IgG vs OPV mucosal IgA -- the transmission asymmetry, verbatim on the page). Build must additionally verify from primary/secondary sources: Behring & Kitasato 1890 antitoxin paper and the 1891 Berlin clinical case (traditionally recounted -- attribute as such); Ehrlich side-chain 1897 + Nobel 1908; Burnet 1957 / Talmage 1957 clonal selection; Tonegawa 1976-78 papers + 1987 Nobel; Glenny 1926 alum adjuvant.
framing_note: This is the FIRM + CELEBRATED anchor of the whole sub-strand: the immunology is real, proven cell biology and the bank says so without hedging. Voice = MECHANISM mode, but every rung anchored on a NAMED person or moment so no rung degenerates into a definition-shell ('what is an antibody?' is BANNED). ACCURACY RAIL: do NOT say a vaccine 'teaches' or 'trains' the body to build a new weapon -- clonal selection means the matching cell already exists and is merely amplified; getting this backwards is the single most common textbook error and the bank must model the correct picture. Second rail: the 1891 Berlin bedside case is the traditional account -- frame it as 'the case history medicine has always told' rather than asserting undisputed detail. Dinner-test payoff: T4 Tonegawa (your body shuffles its own genes like a card deck to invent receptors for germs that do not exist yet). DISTRACTOR MINE: the real graveyard of immune theories -- humoral vs cellular as a genuine 19th-c war (Ehrlich vs Metchnikoff, who SHARED the 1908 Nobel), the instructionist 'template' theory of antibody formation (Pauling's, seriously held and wrong), miasma, spontaneous generation; plus real adjacent scientists (Pasteur, Koch, Metchnikoff, Landsteiner). LANE BORDER: an animal's immune system as a creature adaptation belongs to ANIMAL; science owns the cell biology and the discovery stories.
history_overlap: Internal science-bank risk: any general immunology / germ-theory ladder in the life section will want Behring, Ehrlich and memory cells. This ladder must stay VACCINE-facing (antigen preview, adjuvants, boosters, drift/shift, the IgG-vs-IgA transmission limit); a general immunity ladder should key phagocytes, innate barriers, fever and autoimmunity instead. ANIMAL bank: immune adaptations in specific creatures. COOKING bank: none.

name: Jenner, James Phipps, and the farmer who got there 22 years earlier
scope: The founding story told completely -- the real observation, the real test, the real priority dispute, and the caveat about what the story was later used to prove. T1: on 14 May 1796 a Gloucestershire country doctor scratched matter into the arm of his gardener's eight-year-old son, James Phipps -- the material came from a cowpox sore on the hand of milkmaid Sarah Nelmes, who had caught it from a cow named Blossom. T2: Jenner had been variolated himself at eight and remembered it as an ordeal -- his motive was a SAFER method, not a first one. T2: six weeks later he deliberately exposed Phipps to smallpox matter; nothing happened, and he repeated the exposure. T3: the Royal Society declined his paper and advised him not to risk his reputation on it; he published the Inquiry himself in 1798, at his own expense, on 23 cases. T3: Jenner's own preferred origin theory was WRONG -- he believed the protective agent came ultimately from 'the grease', a horse hoof disease carried to cows by farmhands. T4: BENJAMIN JESTY got there first. In 1774 the Dorset farmer took cowpox from a diseased cow at Chetnole and scratched it into his wife Elizabeth and their two eldest sons with a DARNING NEEDLE; his neighbours hooted, reviled and pelted him at market for putting an animal's disease into people. In 1805 the Original Vaccine Pock Institute in London examined him -- his son Robert, then 28, submitted to smallpox inoculation to prove he was still immune -- and Jesty went home with a testimonial and a pair of gold-mounted lancets. His 1816 gravestone at Worth Matravers names him as the first. T4: Jenner insisted the protection was LIFELONG; it is not, and revaccination became standard within his own century -- the discoverer was wrong about the durability of his own discovery. T5: the word itself -- Jenner coined 'vaccine' from Latin vacca, a cow, and that single word now travels ahead of every later product, carrying the smallpox result with it. The honest position the bank takes: the cowpox observation was real and the eradication that followed was real, AND every later vaccine has to earn its own evidence rather than inherit Jenner's.
source: grokipedia.com/page/Edward_Jenner (14 May 1796, James Phipps age 8, Sarah Nelmes, cow Blossom, 6-week challenge, Inquiry 1798, Jenner variolated at 8, Parliament grants 1802/1807, Temple of Vaccinia); grokipedia.com/page/Variolation (Jenner developed vaccination 1796 to supplant variolation); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Jesty (1774, Elizabeth + two eldest sons, Chetnole, darning needle, 'hooted at, reviled and pelted', 1805 Original Vaccine Pock Institute, son Robert age 28 re-challenged, gold-mounted lancets, Michael William Sharp portrait, 1816 Worth Matravers gravestone). Build must additionally verify: the Royal Society's rejection of Jenner's 1796 communication; the 23 cases in the Inquiry; Jenner's horse-'grease' hypothesis in his own text.
framing_note: Voice = DISCOVERY plus a genuine priority REVERSAL. The stance lean lives in T5 only, and it must be stated as a claim about EVIDENCE, never as a slur on vaccination: Jenner's result is celebrated, and the bank simply refuses to let one 1796 result vouch for products invented two centuries later. ACCURACY RAIL: Jenner is NOT 'the first person to use cowpox' -- Jesty (1774) and probably others did it before him; what Jenner did first was TEST it, write it up and publish, which is the actual scientific act. Say it exactly that way; getting it wrong in either direction (Jenner as sole genius / Jenner as plagiarist) fails the audit. Dinner-test payoff: T4 Jesty and the darning needle -- a farmer, his wife and his two sons, pelted in the market square. DISTRACTOR MINE: real adjacent practice and people -- variolation with actual smallpox matter (the live rival technique), the horse-grease theory (Jenner's own), Sarah Nelmes vs Blossom vs Phipps as attribution traps, Lady Mary Wortley Montagu, Zabdiel Boylston, Benjamin Waterhouse. Never let a stem say 'cowpox protects against smallpox' before asking what Jenner did -- describe the SCENE (a country doctor, a milkmaid's hand, a gardener's boy) and make the knowledge recalled. LANE BORDER: cowpox as a cattle disease is ANIMAL's; the 18th-century English countryside as social history is HISTORY's; science owns the observation, the test and the publication.
history_overlap: HISTORY bank: smallpox in the Americas / 18th-century Britain almost certainly carries Jenner as a milestone -- the science rung must key the TEST and the Jesty priority dispute, not 'Jenner invented vaccination in 1796' as a date fact. ANIMAL bank: cowpox in cattle. Internal science overlap: the smallpox-eradication ladder in this same sub-strand -- keep 1980 out of this ladder entirely.

name: Before Jenner: Montagu, Onesimus, and Boylston's arithmetic
scope: Inoculation existed for centuries before Europe noticed it, and the moment Europe did notice, someone COUNTED. T1: in Istanbul in 1717 the British ambassador's wife, Lady Mary Wortley Montagu -- whose own face was scarred and whose brother had died of smallpox -- watched old Turkish women at 'engrafting parties' open a vein with a needle and rub in matter taken from a mild case. T2: she had her five-year-old son inoculated there in 1718 by the embassy surgeon Charles Maitland, and her three-year-old daughter in London in April 1721 -- the first professional variolation in England, performed in front of physicians she invited to watch. T2: Boston, 1721 -- the Puritan minister Cotton Mather already knew the technique, because ONESIMUS, an enslaved West African man in his household, had shown him the scar on his arm and told him it had been done where he came from. T3: Mather could not persuade the doctors; one physician, Zabdiel Boylston, tried it -- and then did the thing that mattered: he KEPT COUNT. About 250 inoculated Bostonians, roughly 2 per cent of whom died, against roughly 14 per cent of those who caught smallpox in the ordinary way. Numbers, not authority, settled the argument -- and a bomb was thrown through Mather's window for his trouble. T3: the price of the method, stated plainly -- variolation gave you REAL smallpox; 1 to 2 per cent of the inoculated died of the treatment itself, against about 30 per cent for natural variola major. T4: and the inoculated were CONTAGIOUS -- an inoculated person could seed an ordinary epidemic, which is why isolation for one to two weeks was part of the procedure and why several jurisdictions eventually banned it. T4: the ethics rung -- the August 1721 'Royal Experiment' at Newgate Prison, where six condemned prisoners were variolated in exchange for a pardon, then charity-school orphans, and only then the royal children. T4: George Washington ordered the whole Continental Army variolated in 1777; Catherine the Great took it herself in 1768 and put more than two million subjects through it.
source: grokipedia.com/page/Variolation (Constantinople 1717 Montagu; 1721 England and Boston; Cotton Mather and Zabdiel Boylston acting on Onesimus's account; ~250 inoculated in Boston; 1-2% variolation fatality vs ~30% natural; Washington 1777; Catherine the Great 1768 and >2M subjects; Russia banned variolation 1805); grokipedia.com/page/Edward_Jenner (variolation as the risky predecessor Jenner set out to replace). Build must additionally verify before authoring: Montagu's son inoculated in Constantinople in 1718 by Charles Maitland and her daughter in London in April 1721 (Grokipedia compresses this to 'had her children inoculated' -- get the two events right); Boylston's published mortality figures (his 1726 Historical Account); the Newgate 'Royal Experiment' of August 1721; the bomb thrown into Mather's house.
framing_note: Voice = DISCOVERY plus the bank's method soul: the payoff is that BOYLSTON COUNTED. This is the earliest rung in the whole science bank where a tally of outcomes beat the united opinion of credentialled men, and it should be framed as the ancestor of every controlled trial that follows -- it hands directly to the Francis field-trial ladder. ACCURACY RAIL: Onesimus must be named and credited as the source of the knowledge, plainly and without either erasure or modern editorialising -- he told Mather it was done in his country, and that is what happened. Do NOT call variolation 'the first vaccine': it used live smallpox and is a different, more dangerous procedure; conflating the two is the error this ladder exists to prevent. Dinner-test payoff: T3 Boylston's two numbers, 2 per cent against 14. DISTRACTOR MINE: real adjacent people and practices -- Jenner and cowpox (chronologically wrong here, which is exactly why it is a live distractor), Charles Maitland, Cotton Mather, Benjamin Waterhouse, the miasma theory, the four humours, quarantine. LANE BORDER: Istanbul as a place belongs to GEOGRAPHY; the Boston 1721 riot, slavery in colonial New England, and Washington's army order are HISTORY -- science keeps the procedure, the risk arithmetic and Boylston's count.
history_overlap: HIGH -- flag hard. HISTORY bank very likely owns: Lady Mary Wortley Montagu and the Ottoman embassy; Cotton Mather / Onesimus / the 1721 Boston inoculation controversy as a colonial-America episode; Washington's 1777 Continental Army inoculation order; Catherine the Great. The science rungs must key the METHOD (the engrafting technique, the 1-2% vs 30% risk arithmetic, Boylston's tally, contagiousness of the inoculated) and NOT the political or biographical story. GEOGRAPHY bank: Istanbul/Constantinople.

name: The Francis field trial: what a good test looks like
scope: The largest medical experiment ever run to that point, and the fight over how to run it honestly. T1: in 1954, 1,829,916 American schoolchildren rolled up their sleeves as 'Polio Pioneers'; the ones who were not getting vaccine did not get nothing -- they got an injection of harmless culture fluid, a placebo, so that no child, parent or doctor knew who had had the real thing. T2: the man who designed it was Thomas Francis Jr., Salk's own former mentor at Michigan, and he agreed to evaluate the vaccine only on HIS terms: randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled. Salk objected that giving a child a dummy shot in a polio year was indefensible. Francis did not budge. T3: he did not get it everywhere. Some health districts refused the placebo and ran an 'observed control' design instead -- vaccinate the second grade, watch the first and third -- and that arm turned out to be the weaker evidence, because the families who volunteered their children differed from the families who did not. Two designs, one trial, and the blinded arm was the one everybody believed. T4: 12 April 1955, Rackham Auditorium, Ann Arbor -- Francis read the result to a hall of reporters ten years to the day after Franklin Roosevelt died; church bells rang and department stores hung banners. The report gave TYPE-SPECIFIC results, not one headline number. T5: that evening Edward R. Murrow asked Salk on See It Now who owned the patent. Salk: 'Well, the people, I would say. There is no patent. Could you patent the sun?' T5: the caveat that the sub-strand turns on -- a field trial tests the vaccine AS MADE FOR THE TRIAL. It cannot detect what a different factory will do next month at scale. Thirteen days after the bells, children vaccinated with Cutter Laboratories' lots began turning up paralysed.
source: grokipedia.com/page/Jonas_Salk (>1.8M children in the 1954 field trial; declared safe, effective and potent 12 April 1955; Salk tested it on himself and his family in 1953; declined to patent -- 'could not be owned like the sun'); grokipedia.com/page/Polio_vaccine ('The 1954 Salk field trial, involving approximately 1.8 million U.S. children ... 80-90% reduction'; IPV licensed 1955). Build must additionally verify and cite: the exact enrolment figure 1,829,916 and the split between the placebo-controlled districts and the observed-control districts; the Francis Report's own type-specific efficacy figures (do NOT round to one headline percentage); the Murrow See It Now exchange of 12 April 1955 (quote verbatim or not at all); that 12 April 1955 was the tenth anniversary of FDR's death.
framing_note: Voice = the bank's TEST-IT-YOURSELF soul applied at national scale, and the single most important METHOD ladder in the sub-strand: this is where a child learns what a control group and a blind actually buy you, from a real fight between two real scientists. It is also the ladder that keeps the sub-strand honest -- the institutional criticism that follows lands only because the bank has already shown, in detail, what good practice looks like. ACCURACY RAIL: do NOT give a single efficacy number. The Francis Report reported by poliovirus type and the figures differ substantially between type 1 and types 2 and 3; a single rounded headline is exactly the kind of compression this sub-strand exists to teach against. Second rail: Salk's objection to the placebo was sincere and ethical, not vanity -- steel-man it. Dinner-test payoff: T2 (Salk's own teacher overruled him and insisted half the children get salt water) with T5's 'could you patent the sun?' as the closer. DISTRACTOR MINE: real rival designs and people -- Albert Sabin (who opposed Salk's killed vaccine and was proved partly right later), Thomas Francis, Basil O'Connor and the March of Dimes, the observed-control design, historical controls, James Lind's citrus trial, Franklin's blindfold test of Mesmerism. LANE BORDER: PHILOSOPHY owns falsification as an epistemology seminar; science owns what a good test looks like in practice -- keep every rung concrete and inside this trial.
history_overlap: Internal science-bank risk: a 'control group and blinding' THEME ladder (Lind, Franklin's blindfolds, Mesmer, Clever Hans, modern RCTs) will want the placebo concept -- this ladder must key the SALK TRIAL'S OWN facts (the two-design split, Francis overruling Salk, the type-specific report) and leave the general concept to that theme ladder. HISTORY bank: FDR, the March of Dimes and the 1952 epidemic as American social history; also the Ann Arbor announcement as a media event.

name: The Cutter Incident, 1955
scope: The buried story: the vaccine itself gave children polio, thirteen days after the celebration. T1: in late April 1955, children who had just been vaccinated began arriving at hospitals paralysed -- and in vaccinees the paralysis characteristically began in the ARM THAT HAD RECEIVED THE INJECTION. T2: the cause was manufacturing, not concept. At Cutter Laboratories in Berkeley, filtration failed to clear clumped virus before the formaldehyde step, live poliovirus survived into the finished product, and Cutter's own safety tests passed it anyway. Roughly 120,000 defective doses went out under a federal licence. T3: the toll -- about 200,000 children received vaccine from the bad lots; roughly 40,000 developed polio; about 200 were permanently paralysed; 10 died. T3: and about half of that paralysis was not in the vaccinated children at all -- it was in their brothers, sisters, parents and neighbours, who caught live poliovirus FROM the vaccinated child. A preventive shot started an outbreak. T4: BERNICE EDDY HAD WARNED THEM. In 1954, testing manufacturers' vaccine at the NIH, she found monkeys paralysed and sent photographs up the chain; NIH director William Sebrell did not act on the report. T4: Surgeon General Leonard Scheele suspended the entire national programme; the NIH's small Laboratory of Biologics Control was rebuilt into the Division of Biologics Standards, and the federal government took over lot-release testing. T5: Gottsdanker v. Cutter (1958) -- the jury found Cutter NOT NEGLIGENT and liable anyway, for breach of implied warranty. Liability without fault. That verdict is the seed from which the 1986 liability shield eventually grew. T5: the source rung -- the fullest account of Cutter was written by Paul Offit, the most prominent public defender of vaccines in America, in his 2005 book. The bank notes this deliberately: the record is not a secret, it is simply not told.
source: grokipedia.com/page/Cutter_Laboratories (inadequate inactivation and flawed safety testing under federal licence; >200,000 individuals, ~40,000 polio cases, ~200 children paralysed, at least 10 deaths; suspension of the campaign; congressional investigation; creation of the Division of Biologics Standards; Bernice Eddy's 1954 report of paralysed monkeys with photographs, rejected by NIH director William Sebrell); grokipedia.com/page/Polio (the 1955 Cutter Incident 'paralyzed over 200 children'); grokipedia.com/page/Polio_vaccine (~40,000 infections, 200 paralytic cases, 10 deaths; prompted stricter manufacturing regulation); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cutter_Laboratories (120,000 defective doses; 40,000 abortive polio; 56 paralytic and 5 deaths in vaccinees plus 113 paralysed and 5 deaths by secondary transmission; Gottsdanker v. Cutter -- not negligent, liable for breach of implied warranty). Build must additionally verify: that paralysis in vaccinees began in the inoculated limb (Nathanson & Langmuir 1963); Paul Offit, The Cutter Incident (2005).
framing_note: Voice = DISCOVERY/REVERSAL told without a shred of glee. This is the flagship 'institution' ladder and it works only if it is bone-dry factual: no adjectives, no villain, the documented record carries it. ACCURACY RAIL: keep the two toll figures straight. The commonly cited headline (200,000 vaccinated / 40,000 polio / 200 paralysed / 10 dead) counts vaccinees AND their contacts together; the narrower breakdown is roughly 56 paralytic cases and 5 deaths among vaccinees plus 113 paralysed and 5 deaths by secondary spread. Use one accounting per rung and SAY which one -- a rung that mixes them fails. Second rail: this was a manufacturing and oversight failure, not evidence that inactivated polio vaccine cannot work; state that explicitly at T2 so the ladder cannot be read as a claim the vaccine concept failed. Dinner-test payoff: T4 Bernice Eddy's photographs of paralysed monkeys, sent up the chain a year early and shelved. DISTRACTOR MINE: real adjacent people and mechanisms -- Salk, Sabin, Thomas Francis, Leonard Scheele, William Sebrell, Wyeth and Parke-Davis (other licensed makers), and the real rival explanations argued at the time (a bad filtration step, a formaldehyde-resistant virus clump, contaminated monkey kidneys, an unrelated wild epidemic). LANE BORDER: the 1955 announcement and the March of Dimes are HISTORY's; science owns the failure mechanism, Eddy's suppressed test and the liability precedent.
history_overlap: Internal science-bank risk: this ladder and the NCVIA 1986 ladder both touch liability -- Cutter keeps Gottsdanker (liability without negligence, 1958) and the NCVIA ladder keeps the 1980s DTP crisis and Bruesewitz; neither may re-key the other's case. Also internal: Bernice Eddy appears here (1954 monkeys) AND in the SV40 ladder (1962 hamster tumours) -- two different experiments, one person, and the build must keep them as distinct facts, never one merged rung. HISTORY bank: the 1955 announcement and Eisenhower-era public health.

name: SV40: the virus nobody was looking for
scope: A contaminant rode into roughly a hundred million American arms, and the honest verdict is still open. T1/T2: in 1960 Ben Sweet and Maurice Hilleman noticed that the rhesus monkey kidney cells used to grow polio vaccine were developing strange bubbles -- vacuoles. The cells the vaccine was made in were themselves infected, with a monkey virus nobody had a name for. They called it the vacuolating agent; it became simian virus 40. T3: up to half of captive rhesus monkeys carried it, and no test in the licensing process was looking for it, because no such test existed. T3: BERNICE EDDY, again. In 1962 she injected extracts of the same monkey-kidney material into hamsters and they grew sarcomas and ependymomas -- tumours. Her superiors were not grateful. T4: the scale -- an estimated 98 million Americans received polio vaccine between 1955 and 1963, and an estimated 10 to 30 per cent of doses carried live SV40. T4: the MECHANISM, and it is genuinely elegant and genuinely alarming -- SV40's large T antigen physically grabs and switches off p53 and Rb, the two proteins that act as brakes on cell division. That is exactly how it makes tumours in a hamster. T5: and yet. SV40 DNA has been reported in some human mesotheliomas, ependymomas and bone tumours, the studies contradict each other, contamination of the assays is a live objection, and follow-up of the exposed birth cohorts has NOT shown a clear excess of cancer. The mainstream conclusion is that SV40 alone is unlikely to cause human malignancy; a co-carcinogen role alongside asbestos remains argued. The bank says the honest thing: the exposure is not in dispute, and the consequence is not settled. T5: the METHOD rung, which is the real payoff -- the vaccine passed every test that existed. A product can satisfy every requirement on the books and still carry something nobody had invented a way to see.
source: grokipedia.com/page/SV40 (discovered 1960 in monkey-kidney cultures used for poliovirus propagation; an estimated 98 million Americans exposed 1955-1963 with 10-30% of doses carrying live virus; up to 50% of source monkeys endemically infected; large T antigen inactivates p53 and Rb; tumours in animal models -- brain cancers, mesotheliomas, osteosarcomas; epidemiological studies on vaccine-exposed cohorts 'have yielded inconsistent results'); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SV40 (first identified by Ben Sweet and Maurice Hilleman in 1960; Bernice Eddy 1962 induced sarcomas and ependymomas in hamsters; 'SV40 infection alone is unlikely to cause human malignancy', possible co-carcinogen with asbestos, exposed-cohort studies did not show extensive increase in cancer incidence); grokipedia.com/page/Cutter_Laboratories (monkey-kidney culture as the production substrate). Build must additionally verify: Sweet & Hilleman's 1960 announcing paper; Eddy's treatment at NIH after her findings (documented in Bookchin & Schumacher, The Virus and the Vaccine, 2004 -- check the page before asserting).
framing_note: Voice = DISCOVERY into MYSTERY. This is where the bank models intellectual honesty under pressure: the contamination is a hard, admitted fact and the cancer question is genuinely unresolved, and the ladder must not resolve it in either direction. HARD ACCURACY RAIL: DO NOT quote the widely circulated 1986 Hilleman audio (the Edward Shorter oral-history interview) unless the build obtains the primary recording or transcript -- an unsourced quote fails the bank's rails outright, and the published record (Sweet & Hilleman's own 1960 paper; Eddy's 1962 hamster tumours) is both safer and stronger. Second rail: at T5 the mainstream negative finding must be stated as clearly as the exposure -- a rung that implies proven human cancer would be false, and a rung that implies the contamination was trivial or hypothetical would be equally false. Third rail: never let a distractor secretly be the truth on the open question. Dinner-test payoff: T5's method rung -- it passed every test that existed. DISTRACTOR MINE: real adjacent virology -- adenoviruses (also found in the same cultures), the oral polio vaccine AIDS hypothesis (a real, seriously argued and now largely rejected claim), hepatitis B, the Rous sarcoma virus, HPV and cervical cancer (a real vaccine-relevant oncovirus, which makes it a superb live distractor); real people -- Sweet, Hilleman, Eddy, Sabin, Salk. LANE BORDER: p53 and the cell cycle belong to the science bank's cancer/cell-biology ladders -- here the T antigen rung must stay anchored to SV40 and the vaccine substrate.

name: The contested polio-elimination story
scope: Three separate questions the standard telling merges into one. T1/T2: THE SANITATION PARADOX -- polio epidemics are not a relic of the filthy past. They exploded first in the cleanest, richest countries, Sweden and the United States around 1900, and the mainstream epidemiological explanation is that better sanitation DELAYED a child's first encounter with the virus until after protective maternal antibodies had faded, turning a near-universal harmless infant infection into an epidemic disease of older children. T2: Vienna, 1908 -- Karl Landsteiner and Erwin Popper ground up the spinal cord of a boy who had died of polio, filtered out every bacterium, injected the clear filtrate into monkeys, and the monkeys were paralysed. That experiment fixes the poliovirus as a real, transmissible cause and it is the steel-man every later argument has to get past. T3: in the late 1940s American cities fogged whole neighbourhoods with DDT during polio season, because flies were suspected of carrying it. The epidemics came anyway. T3: the minority hypothesis, named and handled fairly -- Forrest Maready's 2018 book argues the pesticide era (DDT, and lead arsenate before it) shaped the paralysis curve; the bank presents it as one named author's hypothesis and immediately gives the strongest objection, which is Landsteiner's monkeys: a transmissible virus was demonstrated before the pesticide era, so a toxin cannot replace the cause, at most modulate susceptibility. T4: THE COUNTING. In 1962, testifying before a House committee, the University of North Carolina biostatistician Bernard Greenberg told Congress that the criteria for recording a case of paralytic poliomyelitis had changed after 1955 -- residual paralysis now had to persist on re-examination, laboratory typing separated out coxsackie and ECHO aseptic meningitis -- so some of the post-1955 fall in the official curve is a change in what was counted. T5: the analytic rung -- three questions, kept apart: did paralysis actually fall? did the definition change? did the vaccine cause the fall? They have different evidence and different answers, and merging them is how both sides get it wrong. T5: the iconography -- the picture everyone carries is a ward of iron lungs, and the verified breakdown is that roughly 70 to 75 per cent of poliovirus infections produced NO symptoms at all, about 25 per cent a brief minor illness, and about one infection in 200 any paralysis.
source: grokipedia.com/page/Polio (about 70-75% of infections asymptomatic, ~25% minor illness, approximately 0.5% acute flaccid paralysis, 5-10% fatality among paralytic cases; faecal-oral transmission, with oral-oral spread 'more relevant in areas with better sanitation'); grokipedia.com/page/Polio_eradication (poliovirus as an obligate human pathogen; paralysis in about 1 in 200 infections; WASH infrastructure and transmission); grokipedia.com/page/Polio_vaccine (1955 licensure; US paralytic cases from >20,000 annually in the early 1950s to near elimination by the 1970s); grokipedia.com/page/Iron_lung (invented 1928 by Philip Drinker and Louis Agassiz Shaw; use peaked in the 1950s and fell after 1955). Build MUST obtain before authoring the T4 rung: the primary hearing record -- Intensified Immunization Programs, Hearings before the House Committee on Interstate and Foreign Commerce, 87th Congress 2d Session, on H.R. 10541 (May 1962), Greenberg's statement. Also verify: Landsteiner & Popper 1908; the 1940s municipal DDT spraying campaigns (e.g. Rockford, Illinois 1945; San Antonio 1946); Forrest Maready, The Moth in the Iron Lung (2018).

HARD ACCURACY RAIL 1: the Greenberg rung may not be authored from secondary or advocacy retellings. If the build cannot obtain the 1962 hearing text, the rung must be rewritten to the uncontested, independently documented fact -- that the paralytic-polio case definition and reporting criteria demonstrably changed after 1955 -- and the interpretive claim about how much of the drop that explains must be attributed to Greenberg BY NAME as his testimony, not asserted by the bank. HARD ACCURACY RAIL 2: the seed figure 'only 0.5-1% of paralytic cases needed an iron lung' could NOT be verified and must not be used unsourced; use the verified infection-outcome breakdown instead (~0.5% of INFECTIONS paralytic). HARD ACCURACY RAIL 3: Maready is a named author's hypothesis, presented with its strongest counter-argument in the same rung -- never as established, never as suppressed truth. RAIL 4: the sanitation paradox is MAINSTREAM epidemiology, not a fringe claim, and should be stated with confidence. Dinner-test payoff: T1/T2, polio got worse as cities got cleaner. DISTRACTOR MINE: the genuine graveyard -- flies as the vector (seriously believed, hence the DDT trucks), miasma, ice cream and swimming pools as suspected causes in 1950s summers, tonsillectomy as a suspected risk factor (a real contemporary hypothesis), plus real adjacent scientists (Landsteiner, Popper, Enders, Weller, Robbins, Sabin). PRESENT, NEVER PREACH: no rung may imply the vaccine did nothing, and no rung may imply the official curve needs no examination.

name: When the vaccine causes the disease: VAPP and cVDPV
scope: The live oral vaccine's real trade-off, stated in full. T2: Albert Sabin's vaccine is not killed -- it is a LIVE poliovirus passed through monkey-kidney cells over and over until it lost its appetite for nerve cells, and it is swallowed, famously on a sugar cube, not injected. T3: because it is alive it replicates in the child's gut, which is the whole point -- it raises mucosal IgA and blocks transmission, and the shed virus quietly immunises the neighbours too. It also means the child is shedding live poliovirus for weeks. T3: VAPP -- in roughly 2 to 4 cases per million doses the weakened strain paralyses the recipient or a contact. For years after wild polio disappeared from the United States, EVERY remaining American case of paralytic polio was caused by the vaccine, which is why the country switched back to the killed injection in 2000. T4: cVDPV -- where too few children are immunised, the shed vaccine strain keeps passing from gut to gut, accumulating mutations, until it recovers full neurovirulence and circulates as an ordinary epidemic virus. In recent years vaccine-derived cases have OUTNUMBERED wild poliovirus cases worldwide. T4: the response -- type 2 oral vaccine was withdrawn globally in 2016 after wild type 2 was certified eradicated in 2015, and a re-engineered novel OPV2, built to be genetically more stable at the reversion sites, was deployed from 2021. T5: the honest symmetry -- the killed injection cannot revert but leaves the gut poorly defended, so a protected child can still carry and pass the virus; the live drops block transmission but can revert. Neither vaccine has both properties, and the choice between them is a real engineering trade-off, not a matter of belief. T5: and the eradication endgame turns on it -- you cannot finish with a tool that reseeds the disease, which is why the last mile is the hardest.
source: grokipedia.com/page/Polio_vaccine (OPV developed by Sabin via serial passage in monkey kidney cells, licensed 1961; VAPP estimated at 2-4 cases per million doses; cVDPVs 'mutated and caused 67 cases in 2025, mostly type 2'; global withdrawal of type 2 OPV in 2016; OPV induces mucosal IgA and blocks transmission while IPV gives weak gut immunity); grokipedia.com/page/Polio (cVDPV outbreaks 'outnumbering wild cases in recent years'; shifts to novel OPV2); grokipedia.com/page/Polio_eradication (wild type 2 last case 1999, certified 2015; wild type 3 last case 2012, certified 2019; 99 wild type 1 cases in 2024; nOPV2). Build must additionally verify: the US switch to an all-IPV schedule in 2000 and the ACIP rationale; nOPV2's 2021 emergency-use listing.
framing_note: Voice = MECHANISM with an unflinching trade-off at the end. This is the sub-strand's proof that scrutiny is not the same as opposition: the bank explains exactly why a live vaccine is BETTER at stopping transmission and exactly what that costs, and lets the trade-off stand. ACCURACY RAIL: VAPP (a rare event in a recipient or contact, 2-4 per million doses) and cVDPV (a reverted strain circulating in an under-immunised population) are two different phenomena -- a rung that blurs them is wrong. Second rail: 'vaccine-derived cases outnumber wild cases' is true of recent years and must be stated with its condition (in under-immunised populations, after wild virus was driven to near-zero) -- stripped of that condition it becomes a different and misleading claim. Dinner-test payoff: T3 -- for years, the only polio left in America came from the polio vaccine. DISTRACTOR MINE: real rival mechanisms and people -- Sabin vs Salk (a genuine, bitter, decades-long scientific dispute), attenuation by serial passage vs formaldehyde inactivation, mucosal IgA vs serum IgG, herd immunity thresholds; and the real adjacent live-vaccine reversion cases. LANE BORDER: none significant; keep the Afghanistan/Pakistan endgame geography brief and mechanism-facing so it does not become a GEOGRAPHY place-tour.
history_overlap: Internal science-bank risk: the contested-polio-elimination ladder in this same sub-strand -- that ladder owns the counting, the sanitation paradox and the iconography; this one owns reversion biology, and neither may take the other's facts. The mutation/reversion mechanism also brushes the science bank's evolution-mechanism ladders -- keep it anchored to the Sabin strains' specific attenuating sites.

name: 1986: what happens when you take away the lawsuits
scope: The legal architecture that governs American vaccines, and the incentive question underneath it. T2: the crisis was real. DTP injury suits went from nine filed between 1978 and 1981 to more than two hundred a year by the mid-1980s, and average claims rose from about $10 million in 1978 to $46.5 million by 1984. Insurers withdrew coverage. American manufacturers quit the business until one or two were left, and the childhood supply itself was in doubt. T3: on 14 November 1986 Ronald Reagan signed the National Childhood Vaccine Injury Act. A parent whose child is injured can no longer sue the manufacturer first: the claim goes to a special court in Washington, argued against government lawyers, paid from a government fund. T3: the fund is filled by an excise tax of 75 cents on every dose -- the person vaccinated pays for their own compensation scheme. T4: the programme has paid out more than five billion dollars since 1988, mostly through settlements in which the government concedes no causation at all. Awards are capped at $250,000 for pain and suffering and $250,000 for a death. T4: Bruesewitz v. Wyeth (2011) closed the last door -- the Supreme Court held that the Act pre-empts DESIGN-DEFECT claims, meaning a family cannot argue in court that a safer version of the vaccine could have been made. T5: the trade-off, both sides stated straight. FOR: the shield preserved the supply, restored investment, and routes genuine injuries to a faster, lower-burden forum than a jury trial. AGAINST: litigation is not only a punishment, it is a DISCOVERY ENGINE -- depositions, internal documents and expert cross-examination are how the public learns what a manufacturer knew, and in every other American product category that pressure is what forces redesign. Removing it removed a source of evidence, not just a source of cost. T5: the accountability rung -- the same Act ordered the Secretary of HHS to report to Congress every two years on what had been done to make vaccines safer.
source: grokipedia.com/page/National_Childhood_Vaccine_Injury_Act (H.R. 5546, signed 14 November 1986 as Public Law 99-660 by Reagan; DTP suits from nine 1978-81 to over 200 a year by the mid-1980s; average claims $10M in 1978 to $46.5M by 1984; 75-cent-per-dose excise tax; $250,000 pain-and-suffering cap; claims to the US Court of Federal Claims before special masters; manufacturers retain liability only for manufacturing defects, inadequate warnings or wilful misconduct; Bruesewitz v. Wyeth (2011) pre-empts design-defect claims; 'over $5 billion in compensation -- often via settlements where causation is not conceded'; critics' argument that the structure prioritises industry stability and insulates manufacturers from market discipline); grokipedia.com/page/Vaccine_Adverse_Event_Reporting_System (VICP administered by HRSA; $250,000 death benefit; provider record-keeping and reporting duties under 42 U.S.C. 300aa-25). Build must verify at authoring time: HRSA's CURRENT published VICP payout total and petition/compensation counts; the Bruesewitz vote and opinion author; and -- before using the missing-biennial-reports rung at all -- the HHS FOIA response underlying that claim (drop the rung if it cannot be documented).
framing_note: Voice = REVERSAL applied to institutions, argued like a lawyer and not like an activist. This ladder must be the fairest in the sub-strand: the 1980s supply crisis was genuine and the bank says so first, at T2, before any criticism lands. HARD ACCURACY RAIL: the payout figure is now OVER $5 BILLION -- do not use the stale '$4 billion'; pull HRSA's own current total. Second rail: settlements in this programme routinely include an explicit statement that causation is NOT conceded, so a payout is not by itself proof that a vaccine caused an injury -- say this in the same rung as the total, or the rung is misleading. Third rail: the T5 incentive argument must be framed as an argument about EVIDENCE PRODUCTION (discovery, depositions, documents), which is concrete and true, rather than a general assertion that companies behave badly. Dinner-test payoff: T4 Bruesewitz -- you cannot argue in an American court that a safer vaccine could have been designed. DISTRACTOR MINE: real adjacent law and history -- Gottsdanker v. Cutter 1958, Jacobson 1905, the swine flu programme's 1976 federal indemnity, the Vaccine Injury Table, the $0.75 excise tax vs alternative funding mechanisms, thalidomide and the 1962 Kefauver-Harris amendments. LANE BORDER: the ECONOMICS bank owns moral hazard and liability incentives as general theory -- every rung here must stay pinned to the documented statutory and case facts, never drift into generic incentive reasoning.

Cutter (1958, liability without negligence) as its own T5 -- this ladder may REFER to it as the ancestor but must not re-key it as a question. ECONOMICS bank: moral hazard, the incentive effects of liability caps, regulatory capture as a general concept -- flag so the two banks do not author the same reasoning. HISTORY bank: Reagan-era legislation and 1980s tort reform.

name: The schedule, VAERS, and the study nobody has run
scope: The methodological heart of the sub-strand: how would we actually KNOW? T2: count the doses. The American childhood schedule of the mid-1980s covered a handful of diseases in roughly a dozen doses; the current one runs to fifteen to twenty vaccines and, counted the same way through age eighteen with annual influenza included, dozens more. The expansion is not disputed by anyone; what it means is. T3: VAERS, the national reporting system, is PASSIVE -- anyone at all may file a report, and nobody is obliged to. A 2010 study by Harvard Pilgrim Health Care, funded by the federal Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, built an automated detector to test how much VAERS was catching and reported that fewer than one per cent of vaccine adverse events are reported. A system that captures one in a hundred can raise a flag; it can never measure a rate. T3: and the steel-man in the very next rung -- VAERS is deliberately over-inclusive precisely so it can catch surprises, and it did: it flagged intussusception after the RotaShield rotavirus vaccine, which was withdrawn from the market in 1999 within about a year of licensure. The system worked. T4: THE GAP. Individual vaccines are tested against controls before licensure. The SCHEDULE -- all the doses, in that order, at those ages, together -- has never been tested against an unvaccinated control group in a randomised trial. The Institute of Medicine said as much in its 2013 review, which found no evidence of major safety problems AND found the studies needed to assess the complete schedule to be lacking. Both halves of that finding are the bank's. T4: aluminium adjuvants, used since 1926, are the specific worry most often raised; the largest test of it to date is a Danish national cohort of more than a million children which found no association with autism, asthma or autoimmune disease. The bank reports that finding as clearly as it reports the gap. T5: why the decisive trial does not exist -- randomising real children to receive no vaccines would not clear any ethics board, so the question is answered with observational data, which can be large and careful and still cannot fully exclude confounding. T5: the recognition skill this whole sub-strand is for -- 'no randomised trial exists', 'it has been investigated and nothing was found', and 'therefore it is dangerous' are three different statements, and treating any of them as the others is the error, whoever commits it.
source: grokipedia.com/page/Vaccination_schedule (schedules now incorporate 'up to 15-20 vaccines by age 18'; controversies centre on cumulative antigen load and aluminium adjuvants; 'empirical gaps persist in long-term studies of combination effects from dense early schedules'; 'debates continue regarding understudied synergistic risks in multi-vaccine administrations'; Danish analyses of over one million children found no association with autism, allergies or persistent asthma from vaccine-derived aluminium exposure before age two); grokipedia.com/page/Vaccine_Adverse_Event_Reporting_System (passive surveillance, voluntary reporting by anyone, >2 million reports, ~30,000 annually pre-pandemic, underreporting named as a limitation, and the rotavirus/intussusception signal that led to product reform). Build must obtain and quote from the primary documents: Lazarus, Klompas et al., 'Electronic Support for Public Health -- Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (ESP:VAERS)', AHRQ Grant Final Report, Grant ID R18 HS 017045 (2010) for the 'fewer than 1%' line; Institute of Medicine, The Childhood Immunization Schedule and Safety (2013) for both halves of its finding; the Danish aluminium cohort (verify authors, journal and year); the ACIP schedules for the two years being compared.
framing_note: This is the sub-strand's PAYOFF ladder and its safest one, because every rung is a statement about METHOD rather than about outcome. Voice = the Feynman virtue applied to the reader's own side: skepticism especially of your own claims. HARD ACCURACY RAIL 1: the dose comparison must state its counting method explicitly and apply it identically to both years (through what age, counting annual influenza or not, doses or injections or antigens) -- an uncontrolled '11 to 70+' headline is exactly the kind of compression this ladder condemns elsewhere, and would fail the audit. RAIL 2: 'no randomised trial of the whole schedule' is TRUE and 'the schedule is unstudied' is FALSE -- large observational comparisons exist. Every rung stating the gap must state the precise gap. RAIL 3: quote the Lazarus line verbatim from the AHRQ PDF or not at all; do not attach to it any further claim about CDC conduct unless that too is in the document. RAIL 4: the RotaShield rung and the Danish-cohort rung are NOT decoration -- they are load-bearing, and an audit should fail this ladder if they are dropped. Dinner-test payoff: T3, a national safety net that catches fewer than one in a hundred. DISTRACTOR MINE: real adjacent surveillance and study designs -- the Vaccine Safety Datalink (active, not passive), post-licensure phase IV studies, case-control vs cohort, historical controls, healthy-user bias, the self-controlled case series; real named systems and their real findings. NO ADVOCACY VOICE: the closing rung must cut in both directions in the same sentence, or the ladder has failed.
history_overlap: Internal science-bank risk: the replication-crisis / Ioannidis sub-strand owns p-hacking, publication bias and peer review generally -- this ladder must stay on vaccine-specific surveillance and schedule evidence. The NCVIA ladder owns the legal and compensation machinery; this one owns the epidemiology. PHILOSOPHY bank: absence of evidence vs evidence of absence as a formal reasoning move -- science keeps it concrete and inside real study designs.

name: Mandates, consent, and the line from Jacobson to Buck v. Bell
scope: Where the science ends and the question of consent begins -- traced through the actual American case law. T2: Cambridge, Massachusetts, 20 February 1902. With smallpox in the city, the board of health ordered every adult vaccinated or revaccinated within five days or pay a five-dollar fine. Henning Jacobson, a Swedish-born Lutheran minister who said an earlier vaccination had harmed him, refused and was convicted. T3: in 1905 the Supreme Court upheld the fine 7-2, Justice John Marshall Harlan writing that a state's police power extends to reasonable health regulation. Note precisely what the Court did and did not authorise: the penalty was a FINE, not forcible vaccination -- Justices McKenna and Peckham dissented. T3: Massachusetts had passed the first compulsory smallpox vaccination law in the United States in 1809, so the principle was already a century old when the Court blessed it. T4: twenty-two years later Justice Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr. reached for that precedent to justify sterilising a young woman named Carrie Buck. His sentence: 'The principle that sustains compulsory vaccination is broad enough to cover cutting the Fallopian tubes.' Buck v. Bell, decided 8-1 on 2 May 1927, and never formally overturned -- Skinner v. Oklahoma weakened it in 1942, but the Court has never taken it back. T5: 1947, the Nuremberg Code, article one: 'The voluntary consent of the human subject is absolutely essential.' Written by judges looking at what had been done to people who could not refuse. T5: the bank's position, stated once and without heat -- the immunology is real, and whether anyone may be COMPELLED is a separate question, answered by consent rather than by data. A person can accept every fact about a vaccine and still hold that no one may be forced. T5: the strongest case on the other side, stated fairly before it is answered -- a contagious disease is not a purely self-regarding choice, and the harm-to-others argument is the serious version of the case for mandates, not a stupid one. T5: the vocabulary rung -- notice when a LABEL is doing the work an argument should be doing.

Oklahoma (1942) weakened the precedent). Build must additionally verify: the Nuremberg Code (1947) first principle, quoted exactly; Carrie Buck's case facts, including the later documentation that the evidence of her 'feeblemindedness' was fabricated.
framing_note: The stance keystone of the sub-strand. It carries the bank's position that MANDATES ARE CATEGORICALLY WRONG, and it earns that position with case law rather than assertion -- the Holmes sentence does the work, so the bank never has to raise its voice. HARD ACCURACY RAIL 1: Jacobson upheld a FIVE-DOLLAR FINE. It did not authorise holding anyone down, and it did not address modern school mandates. Any rung that implies otherwise is false and would hand the critics of this bank a real error. RAIL 2: the Holmes quotation must appear verbatim and be attributed to Buck v. Bell, 1927 -- this is the single most load-bearing quote in the sub-strand and a paraphrase ruins it. RAIL 3: PRESENT, NEVER PREACH, and never sneer. The harm-to-others argument must be given its best form in its own rung BEFORE the consent rung answers it; an audit should fail this ladder if the steel-man rung is missing or feeble. RAIL 4: the slur 'anti-vaxxer' is never used in the bank's own voice; the vocabulary rung teaches the recognition move -- a label that ends an argument instead of answering it -- and must be written so it applies symmetrically, to any label used that way by anyone. Dinner-test payoff: T4, the vaccination precedent used to justify sterilising Carrie Buck. DISTRACTOR MINE: real adjacent cases and doctrines -- Skinner v. Oklahoma 1942, Zucht v. King 1922 (school vaccination), Bruesewitz 2011, Prince v. Massachusetts 1944, the police power, the Nuremberg Code vs the Declaration of Helsinki, religious and philosophical exemption statutes. LANE BORDER: PHILOSOPHY owns autonomy, the harm principle and consent as ethical theory -- science keeps the documented legal record and the medical facts.
history_overlap: HIGH -- three-way flag. (1) INTERNAL science bank: the eugenics / dark-chapters sub-strand certainly owns Buck v. Bell, Carrie Buck, Holmes's 'three generations' line and the American pedigree of Nazi T4. THIS ladder must key only the JACOBSON-TO-BUCK LINK -- the vaccination precedent being extended to sterilisation -- and that sub-strand must keep the eugenics programme itself. Coordinate explicitly or one of the two must drop the quote. (2) PHILOSOPHY bank: informed consent, bodily autonomy, Mill's harm principle. (3) HISTORY bank: American eugenics and the Progressive era; Buck v. Bell as a legal-history episode.

name: Smallpox eradication, honestly told
scope: The one real, complete, permanent victory -- and the unglamorous method that actually won it. T1: on 26 October 1977 a hospital cook in Merca, Somalia, named ALI MAOW MAALIN broke out in a rash and became the last person on earth to catch smallpox in the wild. He lived, spent years afterwards walking Somali villages vaccinating children against polio, and died of malaria in 2013. T2: the last natural case of the deadly form, variola major, was Rahima Banu, a two-year-old girl in Bangladesh, in October 1975. Variola major killed about 30 per cent of the unvaccinated; the milder variola minor, which Maalin had, about 1 per cent. T3: HOW IT WAS ACTUALLY WON, and it is not what people assume. The WHO campaign launched in 1967 did not vaccinate everybody. In December 1966 in eastern Nigeria, William Foege ran short of vaccine and improvised: he mapped every case by radio and vaccinated only the ring of people around each outbreak. It worked better than mass campaigns had, and 'surveillance and containment' became the strategy that finished the disease. T4: the last smallpox death was not a natural case at all. Janet Parker, a medical photographer at the University of Birmingham, died on 11 September 1978 after the virus escaped from a laboratory below her darkroom. A pathogen got out of a lab, and it killed someone. T4: on 8 May 1980 the World Health Assembly declared smallpox eradicated -- the only human disease ever eliminated from nature. T4: WHY smallpox and not measles or polio -- variola has no animal reservoir, always announces itself with a visible rash, and produces no long silent carriers. The virus had nowhere to hide. That is a fact about the VIRUS, not a template that transfers to every other disease.
source: grokipedia.com/page/Smallpox (WHO intensified campaign launched 1967 'which employed ring vaccination strategies targeting contacts of cases rather than mass immunization'; no naturally occurring cases after 1977; official certification of eradication in 1980; the only human infectious disease completely eliminated from nature; variola major case-fatality ~30%, variola minor ~1%; virus stocks retained in two secure laboratories); grokipedia.com/page/Jacobson_v._Massachusetts (variola major 30% vs variola minor 1% corroborated); grokipedia.com/page/Variolation (smallpox eradicated by 1980). Build must additionally verify: Ali Maow Maalin, Merca, Somalia, rash onset 26 October 1977, his later polio-eradication work and 2013 death from malaria; Rahima Banu, Bangladesh, October 1975; William Foege's improvised surveillance-and-containment in Ogoja province, eastern Nigeria, December 1966; Janet Parker's death on 11 September 1978 at Birmingham; the World Health Assembly declaration of 8 May 1980.
framing_note: Voice = FIRM AND CELEBRATED. This ladder is the sub-strand's proof that scrutiny is not opposition: the bank tells the greatest public-health victory in history with genuine delight and no hedging, and it is placed alongside the critical ladders on purpose. ACCURACY RAIL: eradication was NOT achieved by universal vaccination, and the ladder must say so plainly at T3 -- Foege's ring strategy is the documented mechanism of the win, and getting this right is both the most interesting fact in the ladder and the honest correction to the 'vaccinate everyone' template. Second rail: distinguish variola major from variola minor carefully -- Maalin had minor, Banu had major, and a rung that conflates them is wrong. Third rail: the T4 'why smallpox' rung is not a downgrade of the achievement, it is the reason the achievement was possible; write it as wonder, not as a caveat. Dinner-test payoff: T1 -- a hospital cook in Somalia was the last person on earth to catch it, and he spent the rest of his life vaccinating children against a different disease. DISTRACTOR MINE: real adjacent people and strategies -- Donald Henderson, William Foege, Edward Jenner, Rahima Banu, Janet Parker, Henry Bedson; mass campaigns vs ring vaccination vs quarantine; and the real other candidates for eradication (polio, guinea worm, measles, rinderpest -- rinderpest is the one that actually succeeded, in cattle, 2011, which makes it a superb live distractor). LANE BORDER: Somalia and Bangladesh as places belong to GEOGRAPHY; the Cold War cooperation that made the WHO campaign possible belongs to HISTORY -- science keeps the strategy, the virology and the endgame.

Internal science-bank risk: (a) the Jenner ladder in this sub-strand -- keep 1796 out of here and 1980 out of there; (b) the lab-leak / biosafety topics in the COVID sub-strand will want Janet Parker as a precedent for laboratory escape -- coordinate so only one ladder keys her.

name: 1976: the swine flu programme that was stopped
scope: A mini gem, and the sub-strand's evidence that a system CAN catch itself. T3: February 1976, Fort Dix, New Jersey -- a nineteen-year-old army recruit, Private David Lewis, collapsed and died after a night march, and the strain recovered from him looked like a relative of the 1918 pandemic virus. Within weeks President Gerald Ford was on television flanked by Salk and Sabin urging every American to be vaccinated. T4: about 45 million Americans were vaccinated in roughly ten weeks -- and the pandemic never came. The forecast was simply wrong. T5: the programme was suspended in December 1976 after reports of Guillain-Barre syndrome, an ascending paralysis, began arriving in the surveillance system. The lesson cuts both ways in a single breath, which is exactly why the bank keeps it: a rare harm WAS detected and the government DID stop the programme, which is what a working safety system looks like -- and the whole thing began with a confident prediction that never happened.
source: grokipedia.com/page/Vaccine_Adverse_Event_Reporting_System (post-licensure surveillance and signal detection as the mechanism by which such events surface); grokipedia.com/page/National_Childhood_Vaccine_Injury_Act (the pre-1986 liability landscape into which the 1976 federal indemnity fits). NOTE: the 1976 episode itself was NOT verified during this research pass -- the build MUST verify from primary sources before authoring: the Fort Dix outbreak and Private David Lewis's death (February 1976); Ford's 24 March 1976 announcement; the enrolment figure of roughly 45 million; the suspension date of 16 December 1976; and the Guillain-Barre attributable-risk estimate. Richard Neustadt and Harvey Fineberg's official HEW review, The Swine Flu Affair (1978), is the primary retrospective.
framing_note: Voice = REVERSAL, at mini length, deliberately placed to keep the sub-strand from reading as one-note. HARD ACCURACY RAIL: every number in this ladder is currently UNVERIFIED -- the build must source the enrolment figure, the suspension date and any Guillain-Barre risk estimate from primary documents, and must drop any rung it cannot source rather than round or approximate. Second rail: do not present this as a scandal. The honest reading is that surveillance worked, the government acted on it, and a confident official forecast was nonetheless wrong -- all three at once, and the T5 rung must hold all three. Dinner-test payoff: T4 -- 45 million people vaccinated against a pandemic that never arrived. DISTRACTOR MINE: real adjacent episodes -- the 1918 pandemic, the 2009 H1N1 response, the 1957 Asian flu (which Hilleman actually did forecast correctly, making it a perfect live distractor), Guillain-Barre vs transverse myelitis vs narcolepsy (the real Pandemrix signal in 2009-10). LANE BORDER: the Ford presidency and the politics of an election-year health programme belong to HISTORY; science keeps the forecast, the surveillance signal and the decision to stop.
history_overlap: HISTORY bank: the Ford administration and 1976 American politics. Internal science-bank risk: the schedule/VAERS ladder in this sub-strand owns post-licensure surveillance as a system -- this ladder keys the 1976 episode specifically and must not restate the general point about passive reporting.
